Rankings use an Elo rating built from completed matches across every circuit, so all teams share one leaderboard. This ranking is in beta and may change as it is tuned.
A team appears after playing at least 5 rated series in the last 180 days, with a match in the last 90 days. Teams that stop playing drop off until they return.
Elo compares a match result with what the ratings predict. Beating a stronger team earns more points; losing to a weaker team costs more. Expected results usually move ratings less.
Teams from different regions and circuits meet less often, so their ratings are linked through fewer matches. Treat small gaps as close, and the W–L record as context for the rating.
